picks.headline: New AI tool maps the hidden universe of small molecules
picks.excerpt: A new AI model charts the vast, largely uncatalogued space of small molecules, giving chemists and metabolomics researchers a way to identify compounds that current reference libraries miss.
picks.rationale: Freshest item in the pool and a concrete new tool: it extends compound identification beyond existing reference libraries, which directly changes how metabolomics work gets done.

picks.headline: The hard parts of AI-assisted science
picks.excerpt: Ai2 researchers lay out five unsolved problems in AI-assisted science: keeping agents steerable as a project evolves, deciding what to delegate, and stopping AI from amplifying methodological flaws.
picks.rationale: The most actionable piece here — a first-party list of where AI research agents actually break, usable as a checklist by anyone delegating work to them tomorrow.

picks.headline: Transfer learning for genomic prediction in underrepresented populations
picks.excerpt: Google Research describes a transfer-learning approach that carries polygenic prediction power from data-rich cohorts into populations that genomics studies have historically left out.
picks.rationale: A named method attacking the best-known equity failure in polygenic prediction; credible first-party writeup and distinct from the section's recent Google items.

picks.headline: AI may help identify breast cancers missed by mammograms, but clinical benefit remains uncertain
picks.excerpt: A new evidence review finds AI readers do surface cancers human screeners miss, while cautioning that better detection has not yet been shown to translate into better patient outcomes.
picks.rationale: An evidence review, not another single-model claim: it separates detection gains from patient benefit, the distinction clinical AI coverage usually collapses.

picks.headline: The Attention Deficit of AI Revealed
picks.excerpt: A PNAS Nexus study ran leading LLMs through the Stroop test and found they have limited executive control of attention — a gap the authors say is architectural, not just a memory problem.
picks.rationale: Classic cognitive-science instrument turned on frontier models, with a specific, falsifiable claim about architectural limits — adds the psychology axis the section lacked this week.
